(By Sri.K.Prakash, Adv.,)
 JUDGMENT
This petition under Section 166 MV act is filed seeking compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. It is stated that on 18-04-2023 at about 2.15 p.m., the Petitioner was rider on Motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-JB-3051 from Palm Meadows apartment, Varthurkodi towards Kannamangala on Whitefield main road, Bengaluru, at that time, the driver of canter bearing No.KA-51-AA-2770 (hereinafter called as offending vehicle), drove the same with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motorcycle.
Due to the accident, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
He was immediately taken to Manipal hospital, Malleshwaram, wherein he was treated as an inpatient and treated conservatively.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is suffering from permanent disability and is unable to lead normal life as earlier.
It is claimed that Petitioner has spent huge amount for treatment, medicines, conveyance and other charges.
At the time of accident, Petitioner was aged 41 years, working as a Senior Project Engineer at Adarsh Developers, Bengaluru and earning a sum of Rs.70,000/- per month.
Due to accidental injuries, he has lost his earning capacity and income.
As the accident was caused due to negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle, it is requested to award compensation from the Respondent No.1- Insured and Respondent No.2-insurer.
3. In response to the petition notice, the Respondent No.2 has appeared before the court through its counsel and filed the written statement.
The Respondent No.1 has not appeared before the court and he was placed exparte.

4. The Respondent No.2 has filed its written statement by admitting the issuance of policy to the alleged offending vehicle and the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.
Further, denied the contents of petition averments in toto.
It has contended that, the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
It has denied that the the accident was caused due to the negligence of driver of the offending vehicle and contended that the accident has occurred due to negligence of petitioner.
Further it has contended that the offending vehicle was not having valid permit and FC at the time of accident.

It has also denied the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, avocation and income of the Petitioner, and the future expenses claimed by him, expenses incurred by him and disability suffered by him.

Further contended that the compensation claimed is highly exorbitant,
excessive and unreasonable.
For all these, it has prayed for dismissal of the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings, the following Issues were framed :-
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that on 18-04-2023 at about 2.15 p.m. in front of Manipal hospital exit gate, on Whitefield main road, Bengaluru, he sustained injuries, when he was rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-JB-3051 in a road traffic accident that occurred due to rash or negligent driving of the driver of the canter bearing No.KA-51-AA-2770?
Srinivas.R vs Shiva Kumar.R.M on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93194554/
2
2. Whether the respondent No.2 proves that there is violation of the policy conditions and respondent No.2 is not liable to pay any compensation?
3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as claimed, If so from whom and to what extent?
4. What order or award ?

6. In order to prove the claim, the Petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and in support of his case,
two witnesses are examined as PW-2 and 3 and got marked the documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.29.
7. The Respondents have not chosen to adduce any oral and documentary evidence.

8. By considering the available materials on record and the arguments addressed by the parties, I have answered the above Issues as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: In the negative.
Issue No.3: Partly in affirmative.
Issue No.4: As per the final order, for the following:

REASONS 9. ISSUE NO.1:- The case of the petitioner is that on 18-04-2023 at about 2.15 p.m., he was rider on Motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-JB-3051 from Palm Meadows apartment, Varthurkodi towards Kannamangala on Whitefield main road, Bengaluru, at that time, the driver of canter bearing No.KA-51-AA- 2770 drove the same with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motorcycle.
Due to the accident, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

10. In order to substantiate his case, petitioner has examined as PW-1 and got marked the police documents at Ex.P.1 to 8 i.e., FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, spot sketch, IMV report, wound certificate, charge sheet and order sheet in CC.8434/2023.

As per wound certificate, petitioner has sustained fracture neck, greater tuberosity right humerus, fracture greater tuberosity left humerus,
cervical spondylosis with blunt injury and undisplaced fracture of nasal bone.
11. The Respondent-insurance company has contended that it was the negligence of the rider of motorcycle in causing the accident.
During the cross examination the PW1, it was suggested that petitioner was riding his motorcycle in a rash and negligent and dashed against rear left side of the offending vehicle.
Except cross-examination and contention in the objections, respondent-insurance company has not produced any evidence to prove the negligence of the rider of motorcycle.

12. The learned counsel for the Respondent has vehemently argued that the accident occurred due to negligence of the rider of the motorcycle and not on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle,
hence both vehicles are equally held liable and relied upon the following decisions:
Srinivas.R vs Shiva Kumar.R.M on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93194554/
3 2008 ACJ 1188 between Renukadevi and Bangalore Metropolitan Transport Corporation and another.
ILR 2009 KAR 2921 between Bajaj Allianz General Insurance company Limited V BC Kumar and another.
13.

entities.text: Bajaj Allianz General Insurance company Limited V BC Kumar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Respondent no 2 neither proved the said fact by adducing its evidence nor examining any witness to support its contention with regard to the accident occurred due to negligence on the part of rider of offending vehicle.
Further, it is pertinent to note that the Respondent no 2 has disputed with regard to the alleged accident and injuries sustained by the petitioner.
There is no material before this court to show that the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of rider of offending vehicle and not on the part of driver of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, with due respect of above decisions, the facts and circumstances above said decisions are not squarely applicable to this case.
Hence the contention raised by the Respondent no 2 holds no water.
14. There are no materials on record to disprove the Petitioner's evidence and to prove the contention of the Respondent.
The evidence of PW-1 corroborates with the documents produced by him.
There is nothing elicited to disprove the case of the petitioner.
It is well settled principle that Motor Vehicles Act is beneficial legislation, the tribunal need not to go for the strict proof of rash and negligence.
After the investigation, police have filed the charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle and the copy of the charge sheet is produced at Ex.P.7.
Charge sheet prima-facie establishes the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
From all the above documents it is clear that the Petitioner sustained injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred only due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending vehicle.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
15. ISSUE NO.2 :-The respondent No.2 has taken contention that the owner of the offending vehicle has violated the terms and condition incorporated in the policy.

Therefore, the respondent No.2 is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioners and respondent No.2-insurance company is absolved from its liability to reimburse the owner of the offending vehicle.
The onus of proof will be on the person who wants to rebut the presumption.
The Respondent no 2 has not choose to lead positive evidence that its company is absolved from its liability to reimburse the owner of the offending vehicle.
Whatever, the contention raised by the Respondent no 2 in his written statement remains as pleading only.
They have not proved by the Respondent no 2.
It is settled principle of law that the allegation of the fact can be proved by providing evidence or by eliciting something from the mouth of the opponent.
Keeping in view of modes of proving an allegation of fact, again say that the Respondent no 2 has failed to prove his contention.

The offending vehicle was covered under a valid insurance policy, hence fastening joint liability on the Respondent no 2-insurance company Wherefore, the respondent No.2 is liable to pay any compensation to the petitioners.
Hence I answer issue no.2 in the negative.

16. ISSUE NO.3 :- As per Ex.P.6 wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained fracture neck,
greater tuberosity right humerus, fracture greater tuberosity left humerus, cervical spondylosis with blunt injury and undisplaced fracture of nasal bone and the doctor opined that he has sustained 2 Srinivas.R vs Shiva Kumar.R.M on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93194554/
4 simple injuries and 4 grievous injuries.
17. Due to the accident the petitioner has sustained grievous injury.
Immediately he was taken to Manipal hospital, Malleshwaram, Bengaluru, wherein he was treated as inpatient and underwent surgery.
He has stated that at the time of accident, he was working as a Senior Project Engineer at Adarsh Developers, Bengaluru and earning a sum of Rs.70,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries he has suffered loss of income.
He has lost his normal life as earlier and suffering huge loss of income.

18. PW-2 - MRO at Manipal hospital, Malleshwaram, Bengaluru has produced the documents at Ex.P.22 to 25.
19.

PW-3 Dr.Avinash Parthasarathy, Orthopedic surgeon at Sreenivasa hospital, Bengaluru, has deposed that the Petitioner has sustained the following injuries:
1. Fracture neck, greater tuberosity right humerus 2. Fracture greater tuberosity left humerus 3. ACL and lateral meniscal tear right knee 4. Cervical spondylosis with blunt injury 5.
Undisplaced fracture of nasal bone 20.
PW-3 has stated that both proximal humerus fractures were treated conservatively and he was readmitted and underwent surgery ACL - reconstruction and lateral meniscal repair.

Further, PW-3 has stated that now the petitioner complains of difficulties in walking on slope, climbing stairs,
squatting, sitting cross legged, turning and kneeling.
On examination he has assessed the total disability for left lower limb at 47% and to the whole body at 23%.
21. On careful reading of evidence of PW-3 makes it clear that he has not treated doctor.
He has stated that at the time of discharge the petitioner was stable and he has assessed only physical disability and not functional disability.
22. The petitioner has stated that he was working as a Senior Project Engineer at Adarsh Developers in Bengaluru, earning a sum of Rs.70,000/- per month.
He has produced his appointment letter and salary certificate at Ex.P.12 and 13 to support his claim.
He further stated that he availed earned leave from April 18, 2023 to June 24, 2023.
To prove this, he has produced EX P14 a letter regarding his leave.
On perusal of EX P12 to 14, it is evident that he was the employee as a Senior Project Engineer at Adarsh Developers in Bengaluru, earning a sum of Rs.75,742/- per month.
23. During the course of cross-examination, PW1 has admitted that he is still employed and continued to receive the same salary.
The fact has not been denied by the Respondent no 2.

The Srinivas.R vs Shiva Kumar.R.M on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93194554/
5
Respondent no 2 has not disputed the EX P12 to 14 documents but pointed out that the petitioner continued working and received his salary during the period of the accident.

Therefore, the question of awarding compensation under head of future income does not come in this case and he relied upon the decision rendered in ILR 2010 KAR 2439 between Sri Subhas V the New India Assurance Co. Ltd.,
24.

entities.text: Sri Subhas V the New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Keeping in view of the above said decision, I have once again perused the material available on record, EXP14 shows that the petitioner availed earned leave from April 18, 2023 to June 24, 2023 and continued to receive his salary during the period of the accident.
However, the petitioner has not produced any documents to substantiate that due to the accidental injuries, he is unable to do his work as before and suffering huge loss of income.
Therefore, as rightly contended by the Respondent no 2, the petitioner has continued his job and received his salary during the period of the accident without suffering any loss of income.
Therefore the question of awarding compensation towards loss of future income does not arise in this case.
Based on EX P12 to EX P14, the income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.75,742/- per month.

25. This tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner who sustained the injuries is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
26. Pain and sufferings:

So far as the compensation under non-pecuniary damages are concerned,
considering the fact that the Petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and was treated an inpatient which caused him to immeasurable mental agony and pain, I am of the opinion that an amount of .40,000/- would be just and fair compensation under the head pain and sufferings.
27. Loss of amenities of life:
For loss of amenities of life undoubtedly Petitioner is sure to suffer in his day today activities and face hardships.
Hence, Petitioner is awarded .25,000/- under loss of amenities of life.
28. Medical expenses:
Under the pecuniary damages, expenses related to treatment, hospitalization and medicines, the Petitioner has produced medical bills at Ex.P.20 amounting to Rs.1,17,538/-.
The learned counsel for respondent No.2 agrued in the written submission that bills at Sl.No.18 to 25 in Ex.P.20 are IP bills, these are already included in the final bill.
The patient name is not reflected in sl. no.40 bill.
Therefore, these cannot be considered.
29. Further, the learned counsel stated in his written arguments that the actual amount spent by the petitioner on medical expenses was already reimbursed under a family health insurance plan.

Therefore, the petitioner is not entitled to reimburse under a family health insurance plan and to support his version, he relied upon a citation rendered in 2010 ACJ to 2742 between Binup Kumar R. Vs. Prabhakar H.G. and another.

entities.text: Binup Kumar R. Vs. Prabhakar H.G. and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 30. Considering the contention raised by the respondent No.2 and the above said decision, the medical bills were reviewed once again.
It was found that the bills at sl.no.18 to 23 in Ex.P.20, are not advance bills, nor are they included in the final bills as contended by the respondent No.2.
Srinivas.R vs Shiva Kumar.

R.M on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93194554/
6 31.
Further on perusal of sl.no.1 to 6, it appears that the petitioner has not claimed any reimbursed amount.
The claim pertains only to the balance amount, which was paid out of pocket.
32. Further on perusal of sl.no.40 it appears that the patient's name is not mentioned.
As correctly argued by the respondent No.2, the said bill does not relate to the treatment of accidental injuries and is therefore excluded from consideration.

On perusal of medical bills, it appears that the petitioner has incurred expenses amounting to Rs. 1,12,538/- Accordingly, the Petitioner is awarded compensation of .1,12,538/- towards Medical Expenses.
33.
Future medical expenses:
PW-2 has stated that the petitioner needs excision of upper pole of patella and repair of quadriceps mechanism prodcedures which will cost Rs.80,000/- .
But he has not produced any estimation report.
In the absence of material evidence, it is just and reasonable to award Rs. 30,000/- towards future medical expenses.
34. Conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges:

Ex.P.19 -Discharge summaries shows that Petitioner was admitted at Manipal Hospitals, Bengaluru, wherein he was treated as an inpatient from 18-04-2023 to 22-04-2023 and again from 15-05-2023 to 17-05-2023 i.e., totally for a period of 8 days.
Therefore, it is just and reasonable to award compensation of .20,000/- under the head of conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges.
35. Loss of earning during laid up period:

With regard to loss of earnings during treatment,
considering 8 days admission in the hospital as inpatient.
EXP14 shows that the petitioner availed earned leave from April 18, 2023 to June 24, 2023, therefore, around 3 months for rest is considered and he took treatment by availing earned leave.
Hence, loss of earnings during treatment is calculated for 3 months.

As the monthly income of the Petitioner is already considered as .75,742/- per month, loss of earning during laid up period would be .75,742 x 3 = Rs.2,27,226/-.
36.
The petitioner has stated that he has incurred a sum of Rs.14,000/- towards repairs and labour charges for his motorcycle and only Rs.4,000/- was reimbursed by his motorcycle's insurance company.
In this regard he has produced Ex.P.16 to 18.
The petitioner has not examined the authorized person or surveyor from the said service center to prove the contents of the same.
Therefore, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation towards vehicle repairs charges.

37. Thus the compensation awarded under the various heads are as under:
Sl. Nature of Compensation Amount No.
1. Loss of future earnings 2. Pain and Sufferings  40,000/-
3. Loss of amenities  25,000/-
4.

Medical expenses  1,12,538/-
5.

Future medical expenses  30,000/-
6. Conveyance, Food,  20,000/-
 Nourishment & Attendant  charges Srinivas.R vs Shiva Kumar.R.M on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93194554/

7 7. Loss of income during laid  2,27,226/-
 up period  Total
Liability:
Respondent No.1 being the owner and the Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending lorry are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation.
However, Respondent No.2 is liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner with interest at 6% p.a.
With these observation I answer Issue No.3 partly in the affirmative.
39. ISSUE NO.4 :

In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos. 1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Claim Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V.Act is allowed in part with cost.
Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.4,54,764/- together with interest @ 6% p.a.
(except future medical expenses) from the date of petition till the date of deposit with the Tribunal.
Respondent No.2 shall pay the aforesaid amount within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount, 25% of the amount shall be kept in FD in the name of petitioner in any nationalized or scheduled bank of his choice for a period of 2 years.
Remaining 75% amount shall be disbursed to the petitioner through E- payment on proper identification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on computer, corrected, signed and pronounced by me in open court dated this the 7th day of February 2025.)
(SHYLA S.M.) II Addl. Judge & ACJM Member, MACT, Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru.
